header: Date: 2026-08-01 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AstraHealth Head of ML), Tom Reyes (Infra), Lydia Chen (Privacy), Samir Patel (ML), Olivia Brooks (Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing benchmark results vs baseline provider (VendorX). Redwood presented updated latency/throughput numbers; overall throughput improved vs baseline for generation workloads but p99 latencies are still higher on some long-turn contexts. Agreed next steps include rerunning with dedicated capacity and tighter batch/cache configs, sharing raw logs, and a security doc follow-up.
topics: Benchmark overview: how numbers were collected
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick 45 minute sync - Marcus will walk through the latest benchmark csv vs vendor x, then open for questions.
[00:18] Priya: sounds good, we only have 45 so maybe focus on the p99 and tail numbers. that's what ops cares about.
[00:27] Marcus: yup, totally. so, quick context — we ran the same prompt set you shared last week, 12k prompts, mixture of short and long contexts up to 1,500 tokens. baseline vendor is VendorX with their managed endpoints. we ran both Redwood hosted and Redwood dedicated-sim on our internal test pool, and we measured avg latency, p50/p95/p99, and tokens/sec.
[00:50] Tom: quick q, you said dedicated-sim, was that actually dedicated GPUs or shared but pinned?
[00:57] Marcus: it was still on our staging cluster, so shared but pinned to a single GPU node to approximate dedicated. not the SLA-backed Dedicated pool, so some variance expected.
[01:10] Samir: ok, what are the headline numbers?
[01:13] Marcus: headline — throughput on Redwood improved by ~18% tokens/sec vs VendorX on the same model (quantized 4-bit), average latency comparable at token level, but p99 for long-turn (1,200+ tokens) is about 2100 ms on Redwood vs 1700 ms on VendorX in that run.
[01:34] Priya: 2.1s p99 is a bit high for us for interactive flows. any obvious cause?
[01:38] Marcus: couple things — batch sizes defaulted to 4 for fairness, but VendorX was doing more aggressive dynamic batching in their managed infra, also they have a different KV cache hit rate — they pre-warm prefixes more aggressively. our prefix/KV cache was configured but cold for some prompt families.
[01:56] Jenna: just to add, VendorX's baseline might be benefiting from model variants and a custom kernel on their infra; we can close that gap with scheduling and dedicated pools.
[02:06] Lydia: also curious about encryption and network hops — could some of the latency be egress or KMS interactions?
[02:11] Marcus: good call — for this run KMS calls were stubbed but not fully profiled. network was colocated but we did see occasional spikes that line up with background autoscaler activity. again, staging sim not perfect.
[02:25] Olivia: do you have per-route breakdowns? our product team wants to know which prompt families have worst tail.
[02:30] Marcus: yep, we included per-prompt family CSV in the shared spreadsheet (link pasted in the chat). short answer: the longest-context summarization prompts have the worst p99, also prompts with lots of retrieval+prompting together.
[02:47] Priya: when you say quantized 4-bit, is that the same quant config VendorX used?
[02:51] Marcus: we tried to match it but there are subtle differences — different per-layer quant packs, and VendorX quietly uses mixed int8 for some layers. we documented the quant profiles in the notes.
[03:04] Samir: any memory/cpu tradeoffs we should watch for if you change batch sizes aggressively?
[03:09] Marcus: yes — larger batch sizes increase throughput but hurt tail latency for interactive requests. There's also memory pressure on GPU which can increase evictions of KV cache causing extra recompute.
[03:22] Tom: can we see results for batch size 1 and 8?
[03:25] Marcus: we have those in the raw results — batch 1 reduces p99 to around 1.5s but tokens/sec drops 40%. batch 8 increases tokens/sec but p99 climbs to ~3s on long turns.
[03:39] Jenna: so tradeoff: if you need tight interactivity, go smaller batches and aggressive prefix caching; if throughput batch-processing, go larger batches.
[03:48] Priya: what about KV cache seeding — can Redwood pre-warm common prefixes?
[03:52] Marcus: yes — we can pre-warm prefixes for high-volume prompt families, that drops p99 by roughly 20-30% in our tests when warm. note our pre-warm tooling is part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[04:07] Lydia: on the security front, we still need the SOC2 summary and network diagram — you mentioned a doc?
[04:12] Jenna: yes, I'll share the SOC2 summary, the network diagram for hosted vs private, and our KMS integrations link after the call.
[04:20] Tom: curious about model fallbacks — if a node is saturated do you auto-fallback to smaller model?
[04:25] Marcus: we have automatic fallback policies by routing — you can route based on latency or cost; for POC we recommend a canary fallback to a smaller quant or smaller model for degraded degradation scenarios.
[04:36] Priya: any regressor tests — quality drop when using smaller model?
[04:40] Marcus: yes we ran MRR and ROUGE-style checks; smaller model loses a few points on long-context summarization, we can share per-metric sheets.
[04:49] Olivia: regarding costs, what was the cost delta vs VendorX for these runs?
[04:53] Marcus: rough ballpark — Redwood hosted runs were ~12% cheaper per token compared to VendorX under our test weighting; with dedicated pooling and caching that could go to ~25% savings.
[05:03] Priya: that saving is interesting but only if we can hit our latency SLO of 1s p99 for interactive flows.
[05:09] Marcus: understood. next step is to try dedicated run with tighter batch size 1 for interactive families and pre-warm cache; that should bring p99 under 1.2s in our projection.
[05:20] Samir: timeline?
[05:21] Marcus: I can schedule dedicated runs next week, depends on availability of an SLA-backed pool. Jenna will coordinate procurement if you want Redwood Dedicated.
[05:31] Jenna: also we'll send raw logs so you can profile spikes — there's a couple mis-attributed spikes that looked like autoscaler pairing.
[05:38] Tom: for the rerun please include a reproducible runbook — we want exact commands to reproduce and tokenization config.
[05:45] Marcus: will do.
[05:47] Priya: switching to security quickly — Lydia had a list?
[05:51] Lydia: yeah, it's mostly about data residency, audit logs retention, and ability to bring-your-own-key. We need to confirm PII handling in our test data.
[05:59] Jenna: we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs are plumbed to the console and can be exported — i'll include links.
[06:08] Lydia: perfect. also on compliance, for Private deployment we need network diagrams and SIEM integration notes.
[06:14] Jenna: noted, adding to next steps.
[06:18] Olivia: any blockers on your side Priya?
[06:21] Priya: need to sync with infra for procuring capacity and confirm samples, otherwise looks doable.
[06:26] Samir: small note — in the CSV I saw a column labelled "KV cash" that I think is a transcription typo, but just flagging that the naming might be off in the notes.
[06:36] Marcus: haha, thanks, we'll correct to KV cache.
[06:39] Jenna: ok, let's do a quick recap and owners. Jenna to share logs and security docs; Marcus to schedule dedicated perf and run batch size 1/4/8 with pre-warm; Priya to confirm dataset.
[06:52] Priya: yep, thanks.
[06:54] Tom: one last question — do you have an easy toggle for quant profiles or will that require rebuilds?
[07:01] Marcus: it's configurable at deploy time for most models; some changes require a quick warm-up but not a full rebuild. we document that in the model profile notes.
[07:11] Olivia: great, thanks everyone.
[07:13] Jenna: thanks all, we'll follow up with CSV and links. meeting adjourned.

Notes: shared spreadsheet link: https://redwood.example.com/shared/benchmark-astra-2026-08-01.csv (placeholder). Raw logs stored in S3 link (redacted).
